data.narrative:
GenFab Co is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Matt Parlmer that has raised $510K to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private robotics and manufacturing firms and 1 public peer (277810.KQ), including private companies such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised as a proxy base value of $510K and applying a typical seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $1.275M. The peer-median method could not be reliably applied due to insufficient data density within narrow peer filters—while 10 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three comparable companies were identified at the same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.08M to $1.47M, centered at $1.28M. This range reflects the single applicable method and its inherent uncertainty band. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for this specific subsector, the early-stage nature of the company limiting operational data, and the sparse comparable set. Additional diligence on revenue traction, IP differentiation, and team experience would be necessary to narrow this range in future rounds.
